It can create a fake systemd service, add init and RC scripts, alter shell startup files, and mark its binary immutable; a cron-based persistence routine appears unfinished. A second mechanism abuses the hardware watchdog: a background worker masquerading as [kworker/0:0] reopens the watchdog device, arms it with a ~30-second timeout, and sends keepalives only while the main process is alive - killing the process stops the feeding and lets the device reboot, after which other persistence mechanisms try to relaunch Tengu. Tengu also overwrites the ELF headers of reboot/shutdown utilities with the string ELFOOD, interfering with normal restart/shutdown commands.

The analyzed sample communicated with a C2 server at 64[.]89.163.8 over TCP port 9931, using plaintext for registration/heartbeat/command output and a custom ChaCha20/Poly1305-like scheme for server commands and updates. It can also fetch a C2-supplied content identifier from an IPFS gateway on the same server and execute or install the resulting ELF or APK. Nozomi assessed the APK path likely targets poorly secured Android TV boxes but documented no confirmed Android victims. URLhaus independently recorded 17 malware URLs at the same IP beginning June 17, 2026, all offline as of July 28; none of the SHA-256 hashes matched Nozomi's published sample hash, so URLhaus's telemetry confirms only malicious hosting at the address, not a Tengu link. Neither source establishes whether the C2 port or IPFS gateway was reachable, or whether the C2 server issued any commands.

1b6fe8bfac4d.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have sounded an alert after finding more than 36,000 internet-exposed BMC management interfaces running IPMI. Of the 36,872 exposed hosts, 24,650 disclose password-derived authentication hashes before login due to a vulnerability in the IPMI v2.0 specification itself, according to a report Lava shared with The Hacker News. The issue is CVE-2013-4786 (CVSS 7.5), enabling remote attackers to obtain password hashes and conduct offline password guessing by capturing the HMAC from an RMCP+ RAKP message response. Dell's advisory states this is an inherent problem with the IPMI v2.0 spec with no patch available.

'More than 30% of the returned hashes were associated with passwords that could be recovered using common wordlists and predictable factory chassis-sticker formats,' said researcher Michael Katchinskiy. The exposure also affected modern Supermicro and HPE servers operated by GPU providers, including systems still using factory-issued passwords.

BMCs are specialized management processors that control power, firmware, remote console access, OS installation and system recovery, communicating via IPMI and Redfish. Because BMCs run independently of the host OS (out-of-band management), a compromised BMC lets an attacker sidestep OS-level controls, survive OS reinstalls, and maintain persistent access. Lava noted that in shared bare-metal AI data center environments, a single exposed BMC can put multiple tenants' workloads at risk.

As of May 6, 2026, scanning found 36,872 unique hosts exposing IPMI on UDP port 623, with over 14,000 in the U.S. and others concentrated in Germany, China, the Netherlands, and the U.K. Nearly 25,000 exposed password-derived authentication material before login; 6,240 BMCs returned authentication material for an empty username matching a weak password, and 2,340 returned data for named accounts (ADMIN, root) matching wordlist passwords. In tests, HPE iLO factory passwords were recoverable within a minute using modern GPUs, and Supermicro factory passwords in about an hour despite being uniquely assigned. Supermicro said it will evaluate improvements to default password policy for future hardware.

Evidence shows threat actors are already targeting exposed BMCs, including ransomware operators leaving an extortion note on an HPE iLO 4 login page; HPE iLO servers were previously targeted as far back as 2020 to deploy the iLOBleed rootkit. Recommended mitigations: block UDP port 623 at the network edge, rotate factory-issued passwords during provisioning, disable legacy/weak IPMI options, restrict BMC access to a dedicated private management network, and apply network access controls limiting reachability to approved administrative systems.

551451f8746f.text:
Apple announced on Monday that it has released patches for dozens of vulnerabilities discovered recently in its operating systems. The company patched 87 vulnerabilities with the release of iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6. The flaws can be exploited to access sensitive user data, fingerprint users, cause a DoS condition, execute arbitrary code, delete files, modify the file system, bypass security, add contacts without authorization, spoof the UI, and escalate privileges.

In macOS Tahoe 26.6, Apple fixed 155 vulnerabilities, including ones allowing access to sensitive user data, arbitrary code execution, security bypasses, and DoS attacks. macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 includes fixes for 138 security holes, while macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 resolves 127 issues. Many of the vulnerabilities were patched across all of these platforms.

According to Adam Boynton, senior enterprise strategy manager at Jamf, 'The one worth a second look is CVE-2026-43810, where Apple notes a remote user may be able to corrupt kernel memory.' Roughly 100 flaws have been patched by Apple in each of its other operating systems: watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS. The latest Safari update fixes nearly a dozen vulnerabilities, including ones that can be exploited to access sensitive user data or crash the browser. The advisories do not mention in-the-wild exploitation. Additional details are available in Apple's security advisories.

c6bbbfac7dcd.text:
Single sign-on (SSO) simplifies access by letting users log into multiple systems with one set of credentials. While this delivers clear benefits to the authentication process, that convenience can also concentrate risk, as the 2025 University of Pennsylvania breach showed. According to reports, attackers compromised a PennKey SSO account and used that access to reach internal systems including VPN, Salesforce, Qlik, SAP, and SharePoint, resulting in the theft of data on 1.2 million individuals.

That does not mean SSO is insecure - when configured and protected properly, it can improve security by reducing password sprawl, centralizing access policies, and easing MFA enforcement. But organizations only enjoy those benefits when SSO is treated as a critical security control.

Start with Strong SSO Passwords: NIST guidance emphasizes length and usability alongside screening for weak/compromised passwords, recommending at least 15 characters for single-factor scenarios, at least 8 characters when paired with MFA, and support for passwords up to 64 characters, plus checking new passwords against blocklists. NIST advises against legacy complexity rules and routine resets, which push users toward predictable patterns. Verizon's DBIR found stolen credentials involved in 44.7% of breaches.

Add MFA, But Ensure It Resists Modern Attacks: Infostealers make it easier to scrape passwords, so MFA should be enforced consistently across users, apps, and scenarios. SMS codes and basic OTPs are better than passwords alone, but organizations should move toward phishing-resistant methods like FIDO2 security keys, WebAuthn, or passkeys, especially for privileged users.

Secure the Assets Behind SSO Login: IdP administrator accounts need phishing-resistant MFA, separate admin accounts, just-in-time access, and monitoring. Signing certificates and keys should have tightly limited access, alerting on changes, and rotation before expiry. OAuth secrets, client credentials, and refresh tokens should be stored in vaults, rotated regularly, and reviewed for excessive permissions. Consent grants and delegated permissions should be restricted, requiring admin approval for sensitive permissions and removal of stale grants.

Is SSO Secure? SSO remains worth using when implemented and protected properly, providing centralized authentication management, reduced password exposure, and support for compliance reporting and rapid access revocation. 'SSO will not cover every sign-in scenario, and it is not secure by default. But when it is hardened properly, it can improve the user experience, reduce helpdesk pressure, strengthen security, and make access easier to govern.' The article concludes by promoting Specops solutions for password policy management and secure access implementation.

50ae19b54319.text:
CAF Bank, which serves 14,000 charities, has suspended online banking while addressing a vulnerability in how third-party software connects to its portal. The outage has created difficulties for some organizations attempting to manage payroll after losing access to their accounts. According to a message reviewed by The Register, the Charities Aid Foundation-owned bank confirmed that online services have been unavailable since July 24 with no immediate restoration date. The bank's communications attribute the decision to reports of suspicious account activity; management stated the problem was detected early and customers were notified of any attempted fraud attempts.

Following investigation, CAF Bank discovered a previously unidentified vulnerability affecting the third-party software connection to the online banking portal, and is collaborating with its technology partner on remediation. The bank emphasized that core banking functions remain operational and customer funds are secure, though online service modifications are underway.

CEO Alison Taylor stated: 'We are working with external experts to fix an issue we identified with third-party software related to our online banking portal.' She emphasized the core bank remains unaffected but the online service cannot reopen until the issue is safely resolved. The bank continues offering phone-based support, prioritizing time-sensitive payments like payroll. Taylor declined to address whether customers would receive compensation.

This incident follows a prior controversy when CAF Bank introduced a new banking platform last year, causing login and transaction problems for numerous customers, for which the bank subsequently apologized. At the close of its 2024/25 financial year, the bank held £1.45 billion in customer deposits.

6c9c0bb38ef5.text:
Securing payment data in the cloud means treating PCI DSS compliance as a continuous engineering discipline. Organizations processing cardholder data across AWS, Azure, or GCP are responsible for data encryption, access controls, network segmentation, and misconfiguration remediation; cloud providers do not cover these under the shared responsibility model. This guide walks through five steps: discover and classify cardholder data, map CDE scope and enforce segmentation, detect misconfigurations proactively, enforce least privilege access, and automate continuous compliance evidence collection.

Retail/e-commerce organizations increasingly process payments across multiple clouds, expanding storage locations, network paths and identity configurations where cardholder data can reside. IBM's Cost of Data Breach Report puts average retail breach cost at $3.27 million. PCI DSS applies regardless of where cardholder data lives; moving to multi-cloud changes how you meet obligations, not whether you must.

Cloud providers secure physical infrastructure, hypervisor, and network backbone; everything above (configuration, application code, IAM, OS patching, firewall rules, encryption) is the customer's responsibility - a provider's SOC 2 or infrastructure PCI attestation does not cover customer configurations.

PCI DSS defines 12 requirements spanning network security, access control, vulnerability management, encryption, monitoring, and governance. In cloud, CDE scoping is the core challenge: every resource storing, processing, transmitting, or connecting to cardholder data falls into scope, and cloud migration expands scope by default without explicit segmentation.

PCI DSS v4.0 became mandatory March 2024, replaced by v4.0.1 in January 2025 with the final future-dated requirements (broader CDE scope definitions, stronger MFA under Requirement 8, customized implementation option, stricter segmentation validation) mandatory since March 31, 2025.

The primary mechanism exposing cardholder data in the cloud is misconfiguration - the 2019 Capital One breach (a misconfigured AWS WAF exposing 100+ million credit card applications) illustrates the risk. Four common CDE misconfigurations map to specific PCI requirements: misconfigured entitlements (Req 1/7), weak/absent MFA on CDE admins (Req 8), hard-coded credentials (Req 6), and insufficient segmentation (Req 1).

Tokenization replaces card data with tokens that hold no exploitable value, potentially removing a data store from CDE scope entirely; encryption (Req 3/4) keeps data technically in scope because keys must be managed. Tokenization is generally preferred for scope reduction at rest, TLS encryption is mandatory in transit.

The five-step approach: (1) agentless discovery/classification of cardholder data across accounts, including catching shadow data stores; (2) mapping CDE boundaries and validating segmentation controls rigorously per v4.0.1; (3) continuous misconfiguration detection rather than point-in-time scans; (4) least-privilege IAM enforcement per Requirements 7/8; (5) automated, continuous evidence collection covering PCI DSS and other frameworks like SOC 2 and GDPR.

Orca Security is positioned as an agentless multi-cloud platform mapping to each step: DSPM for discovery/classification, data-flow mapping for CDE scope/segmentation, continuous misconfiguration detection, risk-scored least-privilege enforcement, and compliance automation covering 180+ frameworks including PCI DSS.

d0cc6882555d.text:
Deepfakes have undermined a fundamental assumption: that familiar faces and voices can be trusted. While most industry efforts focus on detection tools, BlackCloak built Impersonation Protection to validate communication authenticity instead. The company's new circle of trust feature enables executives and prominent individuals to confirm communications from trusted contacts.

BlackCloak commissioned research from the Ponemon Institute revealing that 42% of respondents report their executives and board members have been targeted by fake imagery or video at least once, and 59% say deepfake attacks are very or highly difficult to detect. Generative AI has reduced technical barriers for attackers, and traditional detection cannot monitor every channel executives use - personal phones, FaceTime, WhatsApp, and family group chats - since corporate controls cannot reach these spaces. A 2025 Gartner survey found 36% of organizations experienced social engineering involving deepfakes during video calls; Gartner describes 'episodic attacks' as individual, high-stakes moments designed to manipulate employees into transferring funds or damaging executive reputations.

CEO Dr. Chris Pierson stated: 'You can't spot every fake, but you can confirm the authenticity of communications with your trusted circle.'

How It Works: Impersonation Protection authenticates phone calls, video meetings, emails, WhatsApp, Slack, texts, and other communications in real time. The expanded circle of trust allows members to invite family, advisors, lawyers, assistants, caregivers, and household staff, who download a free app version, register their device, and exchange authentication requests.

Key Capabilities: authentication anchored to person and device rather than message content; confirmation occurs separately from potentially compromised channels; privacy-first validation using device biometrics (BlackCloak says it never stores biometric data); audit trails preserved for both parties.

Availability: Impersonation Protection is currently available as a platform add-on; circle of trust will launch in early fall 2026. BlackCloak will demonstrate both features at Black Hat USA 2026 (August 5-6, Booth #5926).

a5c6d79ae52b.text:
Prescient Security has announced capability expansions to Cait (Cacilian AI), its continuous AI-assisted penetration testing service. The updates rolling out through summer 2026 add attack surface management (ASM), new asset testing types and expanded environment support, extending Cait's reach beyond its initial web application focus.

The announcements follow Cait's general availability launch earlier this year, which introduced an autonomous, context-aware pentester that explores applications before attacking them and delivers exploit-validated, audit-supported findings on a fixed-price subscription or one-time engagement basis.

Expanded environment support: Cait now supports testing across a range of enterprise environments, including isolated testing environments for large enterprises, aligned with autonomous testing protocols.

Attack surface management (Summer 2026): A new ASM capability will give security teams automated discovery and mapping of external-facing assets, identifying what is exposed before using Cait to test it, forming a closed loop of discovery, testing, validation, and remediation tracking within the Cacilian platform.

New asset testing expansion (Summer 2026): Cait is extending its testing reach to additional asset types beyond web applications, broadening the scope of continuous, recurring coverage without separate manual engagements.

CEO Fabrice Mouret stated: 'Most organizations still discover their own attack surface the hard way when an auditor flags it or an attacker finds it first.' Chief Commercial Officer Sammy Chowdhury added that maintaining current coverage 'is the hardest part' for security teams.

219b4f090042.text:
AI-native OT security startup Frenos today announced raising $1.52 million in a seed funding round extension that brings the total raised by the company to $6.4 million. The new investment round was led by Momenta and Exposition Ventures, with additional support from Riptide Ventures. Frenos will use the new funding to expand its customer success team and to grow its AI R&D.

In addition to the fresh funding, the startup launched SAIRA Co-Work, an AI reasoning agent designed to provide evidence-based insights during complex investigations.

Founded in 2023, US-based Frenos has built an autonomous operational technology (OT) security assessment platform that continuously validates the security posture of OT systems. The platform uses a digital twin of the customer's network and SAIRA to run fully simulated penetration tests, validating attack paths, chaining exploits, and prioritizing risks. According to Frenos, its approach reduces assessment time to minutes, has no downtime impact, requires no additional hardware or scanning, and is risk-free.

'Most OT security testing today tells you what's vulnerable, not what's defensible. The question that matters is what path takes an attacker from an exposed HMI to a process they can actually disrupt, and almost nobody is testing for that,' said Dragos co-founder and CEO and Frenos advisory board member Robert M. Lee. 'Frenos is one of the only teams I've seen build a platform that thinks in those terms without putting production at risk to do it. That's a rare combination, and it's why I joined the advisory board,' Lee continued.

6876ad588f5c.text:
Cyberhaven has introduced Cyberhaven Flow, an AI-native data security platform designed to protect data across human and AI workflows. The platform connects lineage, identity, and behavior to safeguard data as it moves through various stages of creation, copying, fragmentation, and sharing. Flow operates across endpoints, browsers, and cloud environments, securing data in both human and agentic workflows, consolidating data visibility, exfiltration prevention, and insider risk management capabilities; security teams can deploy embedded agents to handle configuration, detection, and analysis automatically.

The Shift to Agentic AI: According to Cyberhaven Labs data, endpoint-based agentic AI application adoption reached 60% in May 2026, doubling year-over-year. This means individual agents can execute complex sequences - reading files, querying databases, transforming content, and transmitting data externally - potentially creating significant data loss risks if workflows lack comprehensive coverage. CEO Nishant Doshi stated: 'We are living through the biggest shift in how work gets done in generations.'

Key Capabilities: (1) Agentic AI Security - discovers and scores AI tools and agents across endpoints and browsers, recording activity including prompts, tool calls, and file reads while tracking data context; (2) Lineage and Classification - end-to-end data lineage, AI-powered classification, and unified policies that automatically extend to agent-driven actions; (3) Real-Time Enforcement - monitors activity across endpoint and cloud environments to identify and contain sensitive data movement before exfiltration occurs.

48dee426ee39.text:
Phishing attacks were the dominant method of initial entry for cyber incidents that required remediation during the last quarter, analysis of attacks by the incident responders who were called in to deal with them has revealed, as campaigns have become more innovative around evading detection. According to the Cisco Talos Incident Response Trends report for March to June 2026, published on July 28, phishing accounted for the initial attack vector in just over half of incidents investigated - a significant rise compared with the previous quarter, when phishing represented the initial entry point for a third of incidents. Other top observed initial access vectors included exploitation of public-facing applications and drive-by compromise.

An example detailed by researchers was a QR code phishing campaign targeting organizations to harvest login credentials and further propagate by automatically targeting victims' contacts. The campaign, described as persistent and ongoing as of late June 2026, uses auto-generated victim-tailored PDF documents containing QR codes that direct victims to adversary-controlled Microsoft 365 credential harvesting pages. Attributed to threat actor UAT-11764, the campaign uses two evasion methods: QR codes evade traditional email gateway detections, and the credential harvesting pages are hosted on trusted cloud platforms that might not be flagged. Once credentials are stolen, attackers conduct post-compromise actions including creating email inbox rules for defense evasion and using the compromised account to send further phishing emails. 'By weaponizing existing, trusted infrastructure like SharePoint and Microsoft 365, UAT-11764 can bypass many standard email security gateways,' the paper warned, recommending policies to block/flag QR codes in PDF attachments, phishing-resistant MFA on Microsoft 365 accounts, and monitoring for suspicious inbox rule creation and SharePoint file staging.

Phishing-as-a-Service Kits With Expanded Capabilities: The report noted PhaaS kits are becoming more complex, ranging from toolkits that bypass MFA via the OAuth device authorization flow rather than stealing passwords, to services providing a comprehensive post-compromise toolkit such as searching emails for specific information. Observed capabilities included automated token management, persistent access through Primary Refresh Tokens (PRTs), OneDrive and SharePoint administration, geo-dynamic templates, inbox rule manipulation, cross-account keyword monitoring, and collaborative token sharing, plus advanced anti-analysis techniques including layered evasion and encrypted client-side payloads, highlighting 'the increasing sophistication of modern PhaaS platforms.'

Cisco Talos' recommended protections: implement properly configured, phishing-resistant MFA and tighten authentication controls; configure centralized logging with adequate retention; conduct robust patch management and reduce exposed infrastructure; enforce strict outbound email thresholds to disrupt attack propagation.

d8ff1cb6757a.text: For years, security operations followed a familiar sequence: detect suspicious activity, investigate what happened, and respond before it caused significant harm. That model developed in a threat landscape where defenders had considerably more time to establish facts. In 2019, the average data breach took 206 days to identify and another 73 days to contain, a 279-day total lifecycle. As the time between initial access and attacker movement contracts, security teams operate within a much narrower window, while AI accelerates reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, and campaign execution. Managed detection and response is evolving to meet these conditions by connecting exposure intelligence, machine-speed investigation, and human expertise, helping teams identify credible risks sooner and intervene earlier. MDR must move beyond alert-driven investigations: traditional MDR analysts spend much initial time gathering and organizing information - asset details, vulnerabilities, signal validation, context reconstruction - rather than applying expert judgment. Research with Omdia found 93% of security leaders agree AI improves analyst efficiency by automating repetitive tasks, freeing analysts for complex investigations and response decisions. Preemptive MDR connects exposure and detection: exposure teams see which vulnerabilities, assets, identities and attack paths present risk; detection/response teams see activity as it unfolds. Preemptive MDR brings asset criticality, internet exposure, vulnerability data, and threat intelligence directly into the SOC workflow, so analysts immediately see why an affected asset matters and whether activity aligns with known attacker behavior. The same context can support pre-emptive action, such as surfacing stolen credentials before use or assessing new vulnerabilities against business priorities. Agentic SOC capabilities accelerate investigation: AI agents can examine telemetry, connect related activity, test explanations, and present structured findings in parallel, while analysts review evidence and apply organizational judgment. The same Omdia research found 92% of security leaders believe analysts should retain responsibility for final decisions and 90% view human oversight as essential to accuracy and reliability of AI-driven processes. Connected security data strengthens AI-driven MDR: Rapid7's data mesh brings together asset, cloud, configuration, exposure, event, and alert data in a normalized layer, giving AI-driven investigations connected context without manual cross-tool searching. From faster response to continuous defense: combining exposure intelligence, connected data, AI-driven investigation, and human expertise creates a continuous defense loop where each incident improves future detection and prioritization. Rapid7 will showcase upcoming investments in Preemptive MDR and Agentic SOC at Black Hat USA in Las Vegas, August 3-6, 2026.

b737cd1dfe08.text:
OpenWrt released version 24.10.8 to address CVE-2026-53921, a critical DHCPv6 stack overflow vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.8. The flaw enables unauthenticated attackers to execute code as root on affected devices.

The vulnerability exists in odhcpd, which runs with root privileges. An attacker can send crafted DHCPv6 REQUEST packets to UDP port 547, exploiting insufficient bounds checking in the response buffer. The advisory notes that "embedded hardware commonly lacks stack canaries and address space layout randomization (ASLR), making code execution a realistic outcome on typical devices."

The vulnerability contains two independent overflow paths involving IA options that leave insufficient space in a fixed 512-byte stack buffer.

Remediation: OpenWrt 24.10 users should install version 24.10.8; OpenWrt 25.12 users should install version 25.12.5. Firmware images are available through the OpenWrt Firmware Selector.

As of July 28, 2026, no active exploitation in the wild had been reported, and the vulnerability was absent from CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

The release also included patches for command injection, path traversal, and XSS weaknesses in optional LuCI components discovered through AI-assisted security auditing.

(Author: Swati Khandelwal; Published: July 28, 2026)

1f834ff887d0.text:
Intel 471 announced two new AI capabilities in the Verity471 platform: MCP471 and Agent471. The company emphasizes that as attackers leverage AI to scale operations, security teams must deploy their own AI tools to make threat intelligence more accessible and actionable.

The Verity471 platform converts adversary tactics into pre-attack intelligence and enables proactive threat hunting. The new features operationalize this intelligence:

MCP471 is a connector built on the Model Context Protocol that integrates Verity471 intelligence into existing AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT, and custom workflows. It enables organizations to "combine that intelligence with their own internal data."

Agent471 is a native AI agent within Verity471 that analyzes organizational intelligence across sources, resolving actor aliases and pivoting through data similar to human analysts. It provides "cited and decision-ready" answers and helps teams connect previously siloed information.

Carl Manion, Managing Vice President at Gartner, stated that "Detection and response-based cybersecurity will no longer be enough" against AI-enabled attackers, emphasizing the need for preemptive countermeasures.

Michael DeBolt, president and chief intelligence officer at Intel 471, described the capabilities as "critical milestones" that help analysts work more efficiently while providing "that extra set of hands" security professionals need.

(Published: July 28, 2026)

9e8d38dc21e4.text:
America wants its allies to come together and help it lead the way in defining 6G communications standards, with security and resilience seen as key goals for next-generation networks.

The latest effort to corral international work on 6G comes from the US National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), which says it is pursuing the objectives of a December 2025 memo from President Trump on "Winning the 6G Race."

That memo didn't identify who America is racing against, but it is a fair bet that it is China, which gained a lead during the development of 5G technology. Huawei in particular is understood to hold more declared 5G standard-essential patent families than any other company.

The NTIA says it is launching this initiative alongside more than 20 governments, including several European nations like the UK and the Nordic countries, Japan, South Korea, and Australia. The Nordics are significant as they are home to telecoms equipment suppliers Nokia and Ericsson.

These governments have all pledged to strengthen cooperation on 6G over the next 12 months and beyond in support of greater security, interoperability, and resilience for next-generation networks, the NTIA claims.

"The Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security reflects an unprecedented level of international coordination on the future of communications technology," stated NTIA administrator Arielle Roth. "By working now with trusted partners, we will ensure that next generation networks reflect our shared security interests, strengthen our competitiveness, and drive innovation."

So after President Trump has spent 18 months since inauguration disparaging and threatening America's "trusted partners," the US has decided it would really like their help in becoming the world leader in 6G technology. Isn't that nice?

The initiative lays out specific milestones on strategic coordination over the next year or so, as 6G moves toward commercialization. These include engaging with the telecoms industry to understand the "political and economic landscape" for 6G networks and meetings to identify the potential for more coordinated approaches.

It also calls for a big meeting in 2027 to review joint progress, where the partners are expected to evaluate funding strategies, share information on 6G research and development, assess 5G and 6G technical and cybersecurity risks, and promote common 6G policies.

All of this seems aimed at coordinating positions on the spectrum needed for 6G ahead of the next World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC-27). Scheduled for October 18 to November 12 in Shanghai next year, the conference will consider which frequency bands are made available for next-generation mobile networks.

But it isn't the first attempt at international collaboration over the next-gen wireless standard. The US-UK Tech Prosperity Deal, agreed last year, proposed greater cooperation in a range of science and technology areas including 6G, but this was put on ice by President Trump after just a few months over trade disagreements.

Earlier this year, the Global Coalition on Telecommunications (GCOT) unveiled a set of security and resilience principles it wanted to see baked into 6G from the start. The organization includes many of the same nations as the latest US scheme.

"This is a clear attempt by the US and its allies to shape the 6G landscape before commercial networks arrive," PP Foresight founder and analyst Paolo Pescatore told The Register. "The priority is to embed security, resilience, interoperability, and supply-chain diversity from the outset, rather than repeat the costly mistakes and geopolitical tensions that defined the 5G era. Although China is not explicitly mentioned, the strategic intent is obvious: to reduce dependence on high-risk suppliers and to ensure that trusted nations have greater influence over standards, investment, and innovation. However, this remains a political framework rather than a binding agreement."

The first 6G deployments could arrive as soon as 2029, with the US and South Korea likely to lead in early adoption, according to a report from Juniper Research earlier this year.

Despite this, the exact characteristics that will define 6G networks have yet to be thrashed out. Bodies representing the mobile networks want to see a smooth and cost-effective migration path for their members, avoiding the mistakes made with 5G, while the GSMA has already put it out there that 6G networks may need up to three times the spectrum currently allocated to meet the anticipated demands for data.

(Author: Dan Robinson; Published: Tuesday, July 28, 2026 at 13:49 UTC)

ec5b8afb54e9.text:
You need agents to fight agents. At least that's what David Weston, corporate VP for AI security at Microsoft told his audience during a Microsoft Security launch preview on July 27.

During the event, the Redmond-based company announced a flurry of new AI and security products and initiatives.

First, Microsoft launched Project Perception, a new agentic security system designed to help cyber defenders continuously identify, evaluate and reduce security risk.

Microsoft's Perception coordinates three classes of specialized agents that work together to improve security posture over time: Red agents identify potential attack paths and vulnerabilities before they can be exploited; Blue agents investigate findings, apply security context and determine what represents meaningful risk; Green agents take corrective action and strengthen defenses across the environment.

This is akin to Google's AI Threat Defense platform, powered by Wiz's Red, Blue and Green agents, released in May 2026.

Speaking at Microsoft's launch event, Hayete Gallot, executive VP at Microsoft Security, explained that the global reach of Microsoft means the company see about 100 trillion signals a day. "We sit at your identity, data, cloud, code and even AI level. If you add our security research, threat intelligence and red teaming efforts, you end up with even more signals," she said. "However, if you were to apply an agent to that raw data, it would be very slow and you would get terrible results. That's why we are connecting and correlating all those signals so we can provide a 'security context,' which is organized efficiently for our agents."

Weston added that Project Perception will be multi-model and demonstrated to the audience several "playbooks" based on a set of operations a security operations center (SOC) could face. "We believe fundamentally you need agents to fight agents," he said. Perception will be available in Preview mode for all Microsoft customers from August 3.

Microsoft's First Cyber-Focused AI Model: MAI-Cyber-1-Flash

Gallot also announced the launch of a new Microsoft-made generative AI model specifically designed for cybersecurity use cases, especially software vulnerability analysis. Developed by Microsoft AI (MAI), the model, named MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, is based on the company's internally developed MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model. It has been integrated into Microsoft Security's multi-model agentic scanning harness (MDASH).

According to Mustafa Suleyman, CEO at Microsoft AI, the system is further enhanced by GPT-5.4 and has outperformed competing solutions from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google in CyberGym benchmarking. The MAI-Cyber-1-Flash and GPT4.5 enhancement have achieved a 95.95% success rate according to the CyberGym benchmark. By comparison, OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Cyber scored 85.6%, GPT-5.6 Sol achieved 83.6%, Anthropic's Mythos recorded 83.8%, and Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber reached 83.2%.

Within MDASH, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash handles approximately 90% of queries, identifying and patching software vulnerabilities before verifying that the fixes work. The remaining 10% of more complex tasks are passed to the larger GPT-5.4 model. Suleyman said GPT-5.4 is around ten times larger than MAI-Cyber-1-Flash and can resolve the queries handed off to it. He claimed that the collaboration between the two models delivers stronger performance than competing systems while costing roughly 50% less.

From DARPA AIxCC Winners to Microsoft Security FORGE Lab

The tech firm also announced the launch of the Microsoft Security Frontier Offensive Research and Generative Exploration (FORGE) Lab. The lab will be led by Team Atlanta, the group of cybersecurity researchers that won the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's (DARPA) AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC) at DEFCON in the summer 2025, after Microsoft hired the team to head the new initiative, Gallot said. The FORGE Lab will be headed by Taesoo Kim, who also led Team Atlanta.

During the Microsoft launch event, Kim described the DARPA competition as a "real world AI cyber challenge" and said the winning teams combined cutting-edge research with practical engineering. He reported that DARPA's process encouraged teams to "strike the balance between engineering and high-risk, high-return research throughout the competition," and that Microsoft provided the ideal environment to translate those advances into production given its scale across Azure and GitHub. Kim added that the lab's mission is to "advance the frontier of offensive security research and accelerate the evolution from AI-assisted vulnerability discovery to autonomous security research," positioning FORGE as the bridge from DARPA-level breakthroughs to enterprise defenses.

Launch of the External Red Team Alliance

Finally, Microsoft announced the External Red Team Alliance (EXTRA), a two-pronged initiative designed to broaden the scope of AI safety research. The first piece involves Microsoft's in-house AI red team distributing "unrestricted gifts" to 18 university labs spread across six continents, all in support of AI safety-related research. Ram Shankar Siva Kumar, Microsoft's head of the AI red team, explained in a blog post published on July 17 that the funding comes with no strings attached because the goal isn't to steer research toward specific products or predetermined outcomes. He noted that while some of these universities are digging into the cybersecurity risks posed by AI systems themselves, others explore how AI can be leveraged to strengthen defenses and enhance cyber operations. The initiative's second component focuses on assembling a distributed network of specialized experts who can contribute to red teaming efforts in niche areas, drawing on researchers with knowledge of particular attack methods, languages, cultural nuances, or technical fields.

(Author: Kevin Poireault; Published: 28 July 2026)

65bdff70e9d6.text:
Team Cymru has announced Pure Signal Command, a connected operating environment designed for analysts, security teams, applications, and AI agents to access and act on Team Cymru's internet infrastructure intelligence.

Command integrates telemetry, investigative and attack surface management capabilities, expert analysis, and machine-native access within a unified architecture. The platform creates a continuous path from discovery to action, eliminating fragmented workflows while preserving investigative context and accelerating threat disruption.

CEO Joe Sander stated the platform represents the next phase in their mission, enabling defenders to disrupt threats and reduce response times from hours and days to minutes. The system features natural language queryability and draws from verified, source-proximate data with clear provenance, providing both real-time information and historical context.
